evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'this will take about like five to ten minutes' and 'we can go ahead and provide you an accurate estimate' but never waits for explicit customer confirmation ('does that sound good to you?'); moves directly into probing.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name confirmed (Meredith McMillan), moving day (Oct 28 packing, Oct 29 moving), route (Georgetown to Wall French, roughly one minute drive), size/rooms (two-bedroom apartment, fifth floor to second floor one-bedroom — close to stated destination).
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves straight into logistics probing with 'just to confirm you are moving from a fifth floor two bedroom apartment...' with no prior discovery of customer's concerns or priorities.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment), floor/stories (fifth floor to second floor), rooms (two-bedroom source, one-bedroom destination), walking distance (150 feet from truck to apartment on pickup side; roughly 100 feet at drop-off), elevator access (confirmed reserved), special considerations (antique furniture: buffet, China cabinet, sewing machine), additional items (TV, couch, chairs, patio chairs, bed, dresser). All seven logistics items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Yes — rep explains packing services are charged at hourly rate with material estimate of $217 for two-bedroom, and clarifies customer can cancel day-before if not needed.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes — rep offers 'typical two bedroom apartment usually has 25 to 35' boxes and asks if customer will fall within that range.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full. Rep provides typical range ('three and a half hours to completely move a typical one bedroom apartment with two movers') and personalizes to this customer's move ('fifth floor apartment with a reserved elevator and a long walk... to a second floor, one bedroom apartment with stairs access') and adjusts estimate to 'four and a half to five and a half' hours with $2,329 total budget.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Rep discloses hourly rate ($192/hour for two movers + 26-foot truck), what is included (fuel, taxes, insurance, pads, tools, assembly/reassembly), what is additional (packing materials ~$217, charged only for what is used), explicitly states 'no hidden fees of any type' (no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no disassembly/reassembly fees), and explains time clock starts on-site with 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments thereafter.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After stating the $2,329 estimate, rep asks 'So do you have questions or clarifications around it?' (a probing question, not 'does that feel fair?'), customer says 'No,' and rep immediately continues talking without holding silence: 'No. So but then again that's just an estimate at the end of the day...'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full. Rep states 'if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill and for you know, all of that is included at no extra cost.' Discount terms (starts discounting immediately if late) clearly covered.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full. Rep covers no-deductible framing ('We provide up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages. Unlike our competitors... either charge extra for protection or offer only state mandated 60¢ per pound coverage'), built-in framing ('included in the hourly rate... included at no extra cost'), and no fine-print language ('there are no hidden fees').
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. Rep never asks 'does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. After delivering Two Promises, rep transitions to time-clock explanation ('Okay. And now married it for the time...') without confirming the customer's concerns are addressed.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. Rep asks 'well, do you have any other questions?' — standard empty phrasing that does not specifically probe remaining concerns ('What's still concerning you about this move?'). Customer replies 'No questions right now, but I'll get back to you on like actually going and booking with you.'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False. Rep never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Rep does not ask 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any recognizable close. When customer says 'No questions right now, but I'll get back to you on like actually going and booking with you,' rep responds 'Yeah, go ahead. Alrighty, not a problem. So I'll go ahead, and send you an updated quote, okay, estimate and yeah well thank you very much for your time and you have a good day.' Rep ends the call without making an explicit ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False. No mention of rate lock, no-deposit, or booking guarantee.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None. No booking details (date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, or crew notes) were confirmed. Rep only promises to send an updated quote via email.

top_strength: Jevic thoroughly probed logistics details and delivered a personalized, anchored estimate with full fee transparency, showing strong command of pricing structure and property-specific factors.
coaching_note: Never ask the customer's top concerns before diving into logistics probing, skip the 'does that feel fair' confirmation check entirely, throw away the final concerns check with 'any other questions,' and most critically, never ask for the business — the customer left without an explicit close or booking, leaving money on the table.
